# Vocabulary

Core vocabulary by domain, then set phrases, then the highest-frequency words in
the corpus. The full machine-readable lexicon (2,000 entries with stems, variants,
and morphological notes) is `data/lexicon.json`.

## Core vocabulary by domain

About five hundred high-frequency words used in this book, grouped by theme. Abbreviations: n noun, adj adjective, iv intransitive verb, tv transitive verb, adv adverb, num numeral, part particle, pron pronoun, rel n relational noun, conj conjunction, interj interjection, phr phrase, pos positional. Verbs are cited as bare stems with a hyphen; "imp" gives the second person singular imperative of root transitives; "pl" gives an attested plural; "poss" gives a possessed form when it is not predictable. Nouns without a listed plural are usually left unpluralized or take taq.

## Set phrases and idioms

| Kaqchikel | English | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| -qa chi -wäch | like; be pleasing to (lit. it descends to someone's face) | The thing liked is the subject and the liker is the possessor of -wäch: Nqa chi nuwäch ri wäy "I like the food." Attested in every person in all three sources (nqa chi awäch, xqa chi ruwäch, nqa chi kiwäch). |
| Achike ab'i'? | What is your name? | Answer: Ana nub'i'. My name is Ana. |
| Achike nub'ij awánima? | How is it going? (lit. what does your heart say?) | |
| Achike q'ij wakamin? | What day is it today? | |
| Achike ramaj? | What time is it? | Answer: pa oxi' ramaj, at three o'clock. |
| Achi’a’ xekamisan ri b’alam | men killed the jaguar | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: hombres mataron el jaguar. |
| Aj akuchi' rat? | Where are you from? | Answer: Rin aj Iximche'. I am from Tecpán. |
| At k'o? | Are you there? (called at a door) | Answer: Ja', in k'o. Then: Xape? You have come? Ja', xipe. |
| Ch'o'n chik k'a | See you later; we will talk again | |
| chaqij chi'aj | thirst (dry mouth) | Chaqij nuchi'. I am thirsty. |
| Chi ka’i’ | both | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: ambos, los dos-. |
| chi ke | to them (indirect object) | Plural of chi re. |
| chi re | to him; to her; to it (indirect object) | The relational noun -e/-ichin under chi. Plural chi ke (chke). Nub'ij chi re. "He says it to her." |
| Chwa'q chik | See you tomorrow | |
| Chwa’q xti’anin ri tz’i’ | tomorrow the dog will run | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: mañana el perro correrá. |
| In k'o | I am here (reply to At k'o?) | |
| Jampe rajil? | How much does it cost? | |
| Janila ütz | Very well | |
| Jeb'ël ütz | Very well; great | |
| jotöl rajil | expensive | |
| k'o chi | must; have to | |
| Katam pe | Come here | |
| Ke ri' k'a | So long; bye (lit. like that, then) | |
| Kinakuyu' | Forgive me; pardon me | |
| Kojb'e | Let us go | |
| Kojsik'in | Let us read | |
| Kojtzijon | Let us talk | |
| La yab'iyaj? | Are you out and about? (greeting to someone away from home) | |
| La ütz ab'anon? | How are you doing? | |
| La ütz awäch? | How are you? (lit. is your face good?) | Plural: La ütz iwäch? Reply: Ütz, matyox. |
| La ütz iwäch? | How are you all? (plural greeting) | |
| Loman | So-so (as a reply) | |
| Man nanin ta ri tz’i’ | the dog does not run | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: el perro no corre. |
| Man tab'ij ke ri' | You are welcome (lit. do not say it like that) | |
| Man wetaman ta | I do not know | |
| Man ye’anin ta ri tz’i’ | the dogs are not running | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: los perros no corren (estan corriendo). |
| Manäq chik jun | only, unique | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: único-. |
| manäq rey | dull | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: sin filo. |
| Manäq, man xintz’ët ta ri tz’i’ | no, I did not see the dog | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: no, no ví el perro. |
| Matyox chawe | Thank you (to one person) | Plural: Matyox chiwe. |
| Matyox k'a ri' | Thanks, then (often closes an exchange) | |
| Muqül kaj | bad weather sky | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: cielo de mal tiempo. |
| na yan kan | until later; goodbye | |
| Najin jöb' | It is raining | |
| Q'alaj ri' | Bye; see you; well then | |
| qasan rajil | cheap; inexpensive | |
| Ri Ajaw kachajin k'a | May God keep you (farewell) | |
| Ri b’alam xerukamisaj ri achi’a’ | the jaguar killed the men | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: el jaguar mató a los hombres. |
| Ri taq tz’i’ xe’anin iwir | yesterday the dogs were running | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: ayer los perros estaban corriendo. |
| Ri tz’i’ man xanin ta iwir | yesterday the dog did not run | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: ayer el perro no corrió. |
| Ri tz’i’ man xti’anin ta chwa’q | tomorrow the dog will not run | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: mañana el perro no correrá. |
| Ri tz’i’ nanin | the dog runs | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: el perro corre. |
| Rija’ man ni’anin ta | he does not run | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él no corre. |
| Rija’ man xutïj ta | he did not eat it | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él no lo comió. |
| Rija’ man xutïj ta kär | he did not eat fish | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él no comió pescado. |
| Rija’ nanin | he runs | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él corre. |
| Rija’ xkamisan ri achi’a’ | he killed the men | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él mató a los hombres. |
| Rija’ xutïj kär | he ate fish | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: él comió pescado. |
| Rije’ xekamisan ri b’alam | they killed the jaguar | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: ellos mataron el jaguar. |
| Rin aj Pa Jotöl | I am from the United States | Pattern: rin aj + place. |
| Ruloq'ob'al Ajaw | It is a gift from God (reply to thanks after a meal) | |
| Tab'ana' jun utzil chwe | Do me a favor | |
| Tab'ana' utzil | Please (lit. do a kindness) | |
| Tasacha' numak | Forgive me; excuse me | |
| Xanin ri tz’i’ iwir | yesterday the dog ran | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: ayer el perro corrió. |
| Xape? | You have come? (host greeting at the door) | Reply: Ja', xipe. Yes, I have come. |
| Xar kaj | clear sky | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: cielo azul. |
| Xatz’ët ri tz’i’ | did you see the dog? | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: viste el perro?. |
| Xok aq'a' | Good evening; good night (lit. night entered) | |
| Xqaq'ij | Good afternoon (lit. the sun went down) | |
| Xseqär | Good morning (lit. it dawned) | Often with k'a: Xseqär k'a. |
| Xtutïj kär ri chapkär tz’ikïn | the kingfisher will eat fish | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: martín pescador comerá pescado. |
| Ye’anin ri taq tz’i’ | the dogs are running | Swarthmore Talking Dictionary; Spanish: los perros corren (estan corriendo). |
| Ütz awäch | You are well; hello (statement form of the greeting) | |
| Ütz k'a ri' | All right then; good, that settles it | Closes a turn in conversation; a softer relative of Ke ri' k'a. |
| Ütz, matyox | Fine, thanks | |
